subject.title: [Feature]: Cron job output routing — hard-coded destination for job results (file, channel, session)

question: Should OpenClaw add a first-class cron output target contract, and which file, channel, session, fallback, and status semantics should it support?
rationale: The request adds public cron config/protocol, scheduler-owned file writes, channel fan-out, and hidden session injection, so automation cannot choose the permanent API or security boundary safely.

options.title: Design unified output targets
options.body: Define a single output.targets contract with explicit file safety, channel/session authorization, failure status, docs, and focused upgrade tests before coding.

options.title: Split into scoped follow-ups
options.body: Break the request into narrower file, channel, and session issues only after maintainers define shared status and security rules.

options.title: Decline first-class routing
options.body: Keep prompt/message-tool based routing and document its limitations instead of adding a new scheduler-owned output surface.

recommendation.title: Design unified output targets
recommendation.body: Define a single output.targets contract with explicit file safety, channel/session authorization, failure status, docs, and focused upgrade tests before coding.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent cron session-target and session-management work makes steipete the best available owner signal for the product/API choice.
